title: UAS (Drone) Operations
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 11 covering UAS regulations, Part 107, recreational operations, and airspace access

cards.back:
Weight: <55 pounds
Pilot: Remote Pilot Certificate (16+ years)
Operations:
• Daylight or twilight with lighting
• Visual line of sight (VLOS)
• Class G: Up to 400' AGL
• Controlled airspace: Need authorization
• No flying over people (without waiver)
• Max 100 mph (87 knots)

Under 49 USC 44809:
• Purely recreational purpose
• Pass TRUST (no age limit)
• Register if >0.55 lbs (250g)
• Follow CBO safety guidelines
• Class G: 400' AGL max
• Controlled airspace: Need authorization
• Give way to manned aircraft
• Keep in sight

Automates airspace authorization:
• Near real-time approval
• At or below UASFM altitudes
• Works with FAA-approved apps

UASFM: UAS Facility Map
• Shows max altitudes by location
• Above UASFM = 'further coordination'

Available for Part 107 and recreational

Part 48 (online):
• Part 107: All UAS regardless of weight
• Recreational: >0.55 lbs (250g)
• DroneZone website

Part 47 (traditional):
• UAS ≥55 lbs
• Results in N-number

Mark registration on exterior of aircraft

Broadcasts from UAS:
• Unique identifier
• Location and altitude
• Velocity
• Control station location
• Time mark

Three ways to comply:
1. Standard RID drone
2. RID Broadcast Module
3. Fly in FRIA (FAA-Recognized ID Area)

Initial:
• Age 16+, speak English
• Pass knowledge test OR
• Part 61 pilot with online training
• TSA security check

Recurrent:
• Every 24 months
• Complete training OR
• Pass recurrent test

Carry certificate when flying

Required for recreational flyers:
• Free online test
• No minimum age
• Administered by FAA-approved providers
• No expiration
• Keep proof of completion

Covers:
• Airspace rules
• Safety practices
• Where to fly

May waive certain requirements:
• Night operations (now standard with training)
• Over people (categories exist)
• VLOS operations
• Multiple aircraft
• Yield right-of-way
• Operations from moving vehicle

NOT waivable:
• HAZMAT carriage
• Foreign object drop with intent to harm

NO flying without authorization:
• Class B, C, D airspace
• Surface Class E at airports
• Within TFRs
• Prohibited areas
• Restricted areas (when active)
• Over stadiums during events
• Near wildfires
• Near emergency response

Report within 10 days if:
• Serious injury to any person
• Loss of consciousness
• Property damage >$500 (not to UAS)

NTSB reporting if:
• Death or serious injury
• Midair collision
• Substantial damage to type-certificated UAS

Allowed with:
• Initial/recurrent training completed
• Anti-collision lighting visible for 3 SM

Considerations:
• Maintain VLOS
• Account for reduced visibility
• Know terrain/obstacles
• Check weather visibility

Part 107 Subpart D categories:

Cat 1: <0.55 lbs, no exposed rotating parts
Cat 2: No injury beyond minor
Cat 3: No injury requiring hospitalization
Cat 4: FAA airworthiness certified

Sustained flight over open-air assemblies: Cat 3 or 4 only

Operated by government entities:
• Federal, state, local agencies
• Governmental function required
• Self-certify pilots
• Require COA for NAS access

Examples:
• Law enforcement
• Fire/rescue
• Search and rescue
• Border patrol

Required for most operations:
• See UAS with unaided vision
• Corrective lenses allowed
• Binoculars NOT allowed for maintaining VLOS

Visual observer (VO):
• May assist scanning
• Must coordinate with RPIC
• Does NOT replace RPIC requirement

FAA.gov/UAS: Central information
DroneZone: Registration, authorizations
LAANC apps: Near real-time authorization
B4UFLY: Airspace restrictions
FSDO: Local FAA office
NOTAMs: Airspace activity

Aviation Weather: aviationweather.gov

Framework for UAS operations:
• Information sharing between operators
• Distributed network vs voice comms
• Operators coordinate/deconflict
• FAA provides constraints
• Not traditional ATC services

Future integration tool

Required for:
• Package delivery BVLOS
• Interstate HAZMAT transport

Requirements:
• Part 135 certificate
• Part 91 operations rules
• COA from ATO
• Exemptions as needed

Cannot operate under Part 107 alone

Consider:
• Wildlife refuges/conservation areas
• National parks (often restricted)
• Noise-sensitive areas
• Bird strike hazards (raptors may attack)

Recommendations:
• 2,000' AGL over parks
• Check B4UFLY for restrictions
• Engine-out procedures near birds

UAS ALWAYS yields to manned aircraft

Remember:
• Manned aircraft may fly below 400' AGL
• Helicopters, ag aircraft, military
• Blocked sight doesn't excuse collision
• See and avoid is pilot responsibility

Substantial fines for interference with emergency aircraft

Requires coordination with:
• Airport operator
• ATC facility
• FAA Regional Office

Submit via DroneZone
Evaluated case-by-case
High risk: near manned aircraft operations

Large UAS: May use runways with agreements
